rationale: I'm replacing raw Pearson correlations with a tangent-space embedding. Each subject's connectivity is first estimated with Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, then projected at the Riemannian mean of all subjects' matrices; this is the strongest classic ABIDE pipeline (Abraham 2017). Projecting at a shared group mean removes much of the subject- and site-specific baseline, and keeps the matrix structure that element-wise Fisher-z features discard. The reference mean is computed from the time series alone, without labels.

I'm replacing the Pearson-correlation features with a tangent-space embedding. Each subject gets a Ledoit-Wolf shrunk correlation matrix from z-scored CC200 time series. These matrices are projected at the Riemannian mean of the training fold, so the feature space respects the SPD geometry and removes shared group structure. In Dadi et al. 2019, this was the strongest classic connectivity pipeline for ABIDE. All-zero ROIs are filled with deterministic unit-variance noise so the matrices stay well-conditioned.

This replaces the Fisher-z Pearson features with Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage covariances on CC200, projected into tangent space around the Riemannian (Karcher) mean of the training fold. Abraham 2017 found this the strongest classic connectivity pipeline for ABIDE, because it respects the curved geometry of covariance matrices and reduces noise from short, site-dependent scan lengths. I computed the reference mean myself (a log-Euclidean start, then 3 Karcher steps) to keep each fold to a few batched eigendecompositions, well inside the time limit. The classifier is unchanged; I haven't run this yet, so it has no Dev score.

I'm replacing Pearson correlations with tangent-space connectivity. Each subject gets a Ledoit-Wolf shrunk correlation matrix, and these matrices are mapped into the tangent space at the training fold's Riemannian (geometric) mean. Abraham 2017 found this the strongest classic ABIDE pipeline: it treats each connectome as a point on the curved space of SPD (symmetric positive-definite) matrices and whitens it against the group reference. That removes shared structure and makes subject-specific changes in connectivity easier for a linear model to separate. The reference mean is computed only on the training fold, so nothing leaks from the test fold. Shrinkage also keeps the matrices of subjects with all-zero ROIs positive definite.

I'm replacing Pearson correlations with a tangent-space embedding of Ledoit-Wolf shrunk covariances. Abraham et al. (2017) found this was the strongest classic connectivity pipeline on ABIDE. It treats each subject's connectivity as a point on the curved space of covariance matrices, measured relative to the group reference. This removes the shared structure across subjects and makes the space more nearly linear, which suits the linear classifier. The reference is a label-free log-Euclidean mean over all items, which needs only one eigendecomposition per subject, so it is cheap.
